question.:question/problem:
$$
f(t,z)=⟨12 \cos{\left(t \right)},\,\text{_____},\,z⟩
$$

The vector-valued function $f(t,z)$ above parametrizes the elliptic cylinder defined in Cartesian coordinates as $\frac{x^{2}}{144}+\frac{y^{2}}{9}=1.$ What is the second component of $f?$
question.:question/worked-solution:
Recall that the ellipse $\frac{x^{2}}{144}+\frac{y^{2}}{9}=1$ in the $xy$-plane has the parametrization

$$
⟨x,y⟩=⟨12 \cos{\left(t \right)},\,3 \sin{\left(t \right)}⟩,\quad t\in[0,2\pi),
$$

since

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{x^2}{144}+\frac{y^2}{9}&=\frac{(12 \cos{\left(t \right)})^2}{144}+\frac{(3 \sin{\left(t \right)})^2}{9}\\&=\cos^2 t+\sin^2 t\\&=1.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, for any point $(x,y,z)$ on our surface, we obtain the following:

$$
f(t,z)=⟨x,y,z⟩=⟨12 \cos{\left(t \right)},\,3 \sin{\left(t \right)},\,z⟩
$$

where $t\in[0,2\pi)$ and $z\in(-\infty,\infty)$.

Therefore, the second component of $f$ is $3 \sin{\left(t \right)}$.

question.:question/problem:
$$
f(t,y)=⟨4 \cos{\left(t \right)},\,y,\,\text{_____}⟩
$$

The vector-valued function $f(t,y)$ above parametrizes the elliptic cylinder defined in Cartesian coordinates as $\frac{x^{2}}{16}+\frac{z^{2}}{49}=1.$ What is the third component of $f?$
question.:question/worked-solution:
Recall that the ellipse $\frac{x^{2}}{16}+\frac{z^{2}}{49}=1$ in the $xz$-plane has the parametrization

$$
⟨x,z⟩=⟨4 \cos{\left(t \right)},\,7 \sin{\left(t \right)}⟩,\quad t\in[0,2\pi),
$$

since

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{x^2}{16}+\frac{z^2}{49}&=\frac{(4 \cos{\left(t \right)})^2}{16}+\frac{(7 \sin{\left(t \right)})^2}{49}\\&=\cos^2 t+\sin^2 t\\&=1.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, for any point $(x,y,z)$ on our surface, we obtain the following:

$$
f(t,y)=⟨x,y,z⟩=⟨4 \cos{\left(t \right)},\,y,\,7 \sin{\left(t \right)}⟩
$$

where $t\in[0,2\pi)$ and $y\in(-\infty,\infty)$.

Therefore, the third component of $f$ is $7 \sin{\left(t \right)}$.
